<thought>We need more structural clues. The 1H NMR shows a para‑disubstituted aromatic ring (4 H, two sets of 2 H) and an –CH₂–CH₂– fragment attached to the ring, giving two triplets at 2.62 ppm and 2.77 ppm (J ≈ 7.3 Hz). This pattern fits a para‑substituted benzene where one substituent is an ethylene chain that terminates in a carbonyl (‑CH₂‑CH₂‑C=O‑). The carbonyl carbon would appear downfield in the 13C NMR (~190–200 ppm) and the aromatic carbons would show the typical AA′BB′ pattern. To confirm, I will request the 13C NMR spectrum of the sample.</thought>
